history.summary: Nagara-style temple built in 1204 AD by two local merchants, Ahuka and Manyuka; porch inscriptions record an earlier Shiva shrine on the same spot (the earlier site name was Kiragrama). The svayambhu lingam is worshipped as Vaidyanath ('Lord of Physicians'); local tradition counts it among the 12 Jyotirlingas, though that claim is disputed among Jyotirlinga lists. Renovated in 1786 under ruler Sansar Chand (works led by his family priest Ganga Ram); survived the 1905 Kangra earthquake with minor damage; protected by the Archaeological Survey of India. Dussehra is notably NOT celebrated here, out of reverence for Ravana as a great Shiva devotee. CORRECTION: CSV town 'Palampur' is approximate; the temple stands in the town of Baijnath, Kangra district, ~16 km from Palampur. Coordinates from Wikipedia/GeoHack.

name: Baijnath Temple
town_description: Baijnath is a small temple town in Kangra district on the Pathankot-Mandi highway (NH-154), ~16 km east of Palampur, named for its famous Shiva temple on the banks of the Binwa river.

travel.railway: Baijnath Paprola narrow-gauge station on the Kangra Valley line, ~2-3 km; nearest broad-gauge: Pathankot (~115-130 km)
travel.road: On NH-154, 16 km from Palampur, ~50 km from Dharamshala; HRTC buses and taxis run from Palampur and Dharamshala

visitor_information.opening_hours: 6:00 AM-9:00 PM daily (seasonal aarti/bhog variations reported - verify locally)
